en.body:
## The Grandmaster of Drip's Unforeseen Reception

When **Katsuhiro Harada**, the visionary behind the iconic **Tekken** series, unveiled **Leroy Smith** for **Tekken 7**, the response was electric. This Wing Chun master, exuding an unparalleled aura of cool, quickly became a fan favorite, even inspiring celebrity cosplays. His suave demeanor and compelling backstory resonated deeply, particularly with Black American fans who felt a genuine connection to the character. This overwhelming appreciation led to a unique cultural gesture: fans began 'inviting Harada to the cookout.' For a seasoned developer like Harada, who prided himself on his English proficiency and extensive international experience, this specific invitation proved to be a perplexing, and initially alarming, moment.

> "Now, as someone from my generation in Japan, I was actually considered relatively good at reading and writing English. By then I’d already been to North America over 50 times, had maintained the English I learned for university entrance exams, and had been communicating with people on Twitter in English long before translation apps became useful, let alone AI translation." — Katsuhiro Harada

Despite his linguistic confidence, the phrase 'inviting you to the cookout' left Harada utterly bewildered. His immediate thought was one of dread: 'Oh no… I’m finished.' This reaction stemmed from his recent exposure to the term 'cooked' in online discourse, often associated with negative sentiments or discussions about video games being 'destroyed.' He genuinely believed the invitation was a prelude to harsh criticism or a dismissal of his work, a far cry from the celebratory welcome it represented.

## A Farewell and a New Beginning

This humorous cultural exchange comes at a significant juncture for Harada and the **Tekken** franchise. After decades of dedication, Harada announced he will be leaving Bandai Namco at the end of 2025. This marks the end of an era for the fighting game titan, who has been instrumental in shaping the series' identity for over 30 years. His last project with the company was **Tekken 8**. While he is stepping away from his directorial role, Harada is confirmed to attend the **Tekken** World Tour Finals in early 2026 as a special guest, signaling his continued, albeit different, connection to the community.

## What's Next

Fans can look forward to seeing **Katsuhiro Harada** at the **Tekken** World Tour Finals in early 2026. While his departure from Bandai Namco at the end of 2025 signifies a new chapter, his enduring legacy and impact on the **Tekken** series are undeniable.

content_raw: Katsuhiro Harada, former director of the Tekken series, opened up about a hilarious misunderstanding he had with his international fans after revealing Leroy Smith for Tekken 7 . Leroy Smith is genuinely one of the coolest characters to ever join the Tekken universe. The Wing Chun practitioner was an instant hit when he was first revealed in Tekken 7, even inspiring cosplays from celebrities like T-Pain . In fact, the ‘Grandmaster of Drip’ was so well-received that Black American fans started ‘inviting Harada to the cookout,’ leaving the Japanese game director extremely confused. Harada opened up about the humorous exchange in response to a fan on X, who shared a clip from 1985 cult classic The Last Dragon, arguing that Tekken must’ve been inspired by the martial arts movie and Black culture. In his reply, Harada revealed that after Leroy was announced in 2019, he received a message from the American fan community: “Can we invite you to the cookout for making an awesome character like this?” “Now, as someone from my generation in Japan, I was actually considered relatively good at reading and writing English. By then I’d already been to North America over 50 times, had maintained the English I learned for university entrance exams, and had been communicating with people on Twitter in English long before translation apps became useful, let alone AI translation,” he prefaced. “But honestly… When I saw that sentence, I had absolutely no idea what it meant. In fact, my very first reaction was: ‘Oh no… I’m finished.’” Harada explained that, at the time, he’d been seeing the word ‘cooked’ a lot online, as well as reading articles that were “spreading hate toward video games.” Having learned to associate the word “cooked” with terms like “destroyed,” he was under the impression that fans hated Leroy. “For one terrifying moment, I read it as: ‘Hey… we… we… can invite you to a party where we’re going to beat you up and roast you?’” he continued. “Even though I thought I knew America pretty well, I genuinely wondered if I’d somehow pressed some invisible cultural button that I wasn’t supposed to touch.” Luckily, someone eventually explained the concept of getting invited to the cookout. Harada explained that it was like receiving “one of the highest compliments possible — basically saying, ‘You’re someone we’d trust enough to invite to our close-knit family BBQ, where only real friends and loved ones are welcome.’ “That explanation was a huge relief,” he continued. “Then they started showing me BBQ equipment and ingredients, and I was absolutely shocked that everything was several times bigger than what we have in Japan. Sure, I expected the smoker grills to be huge. But even the tongs and spatulas were enormous, and the meat looked like something I’d only ever seen as loot in an MMORPG. “Looking back now, I honestly regret not immediately flying to the U.S. and accepting an invitation to one of those community cookouts.
